audit.whatIsWrong: Six separate strings credit Irelia with 'passive armor shred' — early, mid, whys[2], whys[5], spikes[1].text and wants.foe[0].
audit.why: Irelia has no resistance reduction anywhere in her kit. Ionian Fervor is 'stacking bonus Attack Speed' when she strikes enemies with spells, plus bonus damage on hit at maximum stacks. A Nasus told his armour is being shredded will buy the wrong item and misread why his HP bar is falling; the real answer is raw attack speed, which is precisely the stat Wither takes away. Fixing this turns a misdiagnosis into the reason his W is the answer.
audit.corrected: All six replaced with Ionian Fervor's stacking attack speed, and the Wither counter made explicit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance is referred to only as 'W block' and 'a fat Q she can just block with W', with no explanation of what it blocks.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Siphoning Strike is physical. A stacked Nasus Q dumped into a charging Defiant Dance is the single most expensive mistake available in this lane — it is his longest-invested resource landing into the one window that is built to eat it. Naming the damage type turns a vague 'don't' into a rule the player can apply.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, the Levels 4-5 stage, early, whys[4] and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Her Q resets' is asserted repeatedly but the reset condition is never given, so the player cannot deny it.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'If the target is Marked or dies to Bladesurge, its cooldown refreshes.' Two conditions, both deniable — thinning the wave removes the dying-minion resets, and Flawless Duet is what applies the Mark. That is why fighting in a big wave is fatal and why the E stun is what actually chains her damage together.
audit.corrected: Reset condition spelled out in dosFull, dontsFull and whys[1]; the E-Marks-then-Q-refreshes chain named in breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defect list: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. breakdown.cooldowns listed Flawless Duet twice and gave no numbers.
audit.why: Defiant Dance is 20/18/16/14/12 and Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 — those are the two longest things she has in lane and the only two windows worth waiting for. Bladesurge at 10s and refreshing is not a cooldown you wait out.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with both real numbers and what each one does.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vanguard's Edge is never mentioned, and the defect list confirms none of Irelia's abilities are named in the content layer.
audit.why: Vanguard's Edge leaves a wall of blades that damages and slows anything walking through it. Nasus has no dash, so in a splitpush duel — which the late-game text tells him to seek — that wall is a cage he must walk through while slowed. It is the one part of her kit that specifically punishes a dashless champion.
audit.corrected: Added to the late-game text; Bladesurge, Defiant Dance, Flawless Duet and Ionian Fervor named throughout.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds line, despite _missing-interactions.json flagging needs-antiheal for this pairing.
audit.why: Bladesurge heals Irelia, and it refreshes off Marked or dying targets, so in a long duel she heals on a loop. The late-game text sells an extended fight as the win condition without mentioning the item that makes it one.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds added to the late-game text.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[6] '2+ items' is side 'Skill' while its why says 'you out-duel Irelia on cooldown', and content win[6] is 'Nasus'.
audit.why: Both layers describe a Nasus-favoured stage; 'Skill' contradicts them.
suspectNames flagged "Spirit Fire's" in late. False positive — Spirit Fire is Nasus's real E name per the kit file; the flag is the possessive apostrophe. No edit made.

edits.after: Still Irelia's window — Defiant Dance is 20s at rank 1 and soaks physical damage while she charges it, so a fat Siphoning Strike dumped into that charge is simply thrown away.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are genuinely even — neither of us wants to commit, so just last-hit with Q and chunk the wave with Spirit Fire for stacks and a little armor shred on her. The danger spikes the instant she hits 2: her Q resets through the minion line to gap-close, and with E stun plus passive shred she out-trades you hard. Do not throw a fat Q she can just block with W, and never sit in her Q-dash range without Wither — at this stage you have no kiting tool and your lifesteal alone won't out-heal her combo.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are genuinely even — neither of us wants to commit, so just last-hit with Q and chunk the wave with Spirit Fire for stacks and a little armor shred on her. The danger spikes the instant she hits 2: Bladesurge (Q) refreshes off dying minions to gap-close, and with Flawless Duet (E) stun plus Ionian Fervor attack speed she out-trades you hard. Never dump a fat Siphoning Strike into a charging Defiant Dance (W), which soaks physical damage, and never sit in Bladesurge range without Wither.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are the worst of it: she has Wither's answer (Q dashes) before you have Wither's payoff, and her armor shred makes your fat HP feel like paper. Play not to die — shove with Spirit Fire, soak Q stacks, and give up the plates if you must. Six is your lifeline: Fury of the Sands' bonus HP and AoE plus Wither lets you survive or even flip a committed all-in. Slow her with W the moment she dashes in so her Q-resets can't kite you, then R and grind. You still don't own the lane at 6, but you stop dying for free.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are the worst of it: she has Wither's answer (Bladesurge) before you have Wither's payoff, and Ionian Fervor's stacking attack speed makes your fat HP feel like paper. Play not to die — shove with Spirit Fire, soak Q stacks, and give up the plates if you must. Six is your lifeline: Fury of the Sands plus Wither lets you survive or even flip a committed all-in, because Wither attacks the exact stat her passive builds. Slow her the frame she dashes in, then R and grind. You stop dying for free.

edits.before: This is where the matchup inverts. Once your Q is stacked and you've got Sheen or a Trinity component, Wither turns her into a sitting duck — point-and-click slow kills her dash-kite, your empowered Q burst chunks her squishy duelist HP, and Spirit Fire's armor shred plus your lifesteal out-grinds anything she throws. She has no percent-HP or true damage, so your fat bar holds and you win every extended fight. Splitpush with R up and force her to answer you 1v1, or peel for your carries — late game, you are the monster she couldn't close out.
edits.after: This is where the matchup inverts. Once your Q is stacked and you've got Sheen or a Trinity component, Wither turns her into a sitting duck — its attack-speed half erases Ionian Fervor, your empowered Q burst chunks her squishy duelist HP, and Spirit Fire's armor shred out-grinds anything she throws. Buy Grievous Wounds, because Bladesurge heals her on every dash, and respect Vanguard's Edge: the blade wall slows anything walking through it and you have no dash to skip it. Otherwise you win every extended fight.

notes: The 'passive armor shred' error is the important one here — it appears six times and it is not a wording slip, it is a wrong mental model of why Nasus loses levels 3-5. Once it is correctly identified as Ionian Fervor's stacking attack speed, Wither stops being generic peel and becomes the direct counter to her scaling stat, which is what the rest of the entry is already trying to say.
